canonical_definition: Algorithmic Reasoning is the ability to execute, learn, and generalize multi-step algorithmic procedures or symbolic manipulations to solve problems, often involving tasks like lexicographic sorting, arithmetic computations, sequence operations, or procedural logic. It emphasizes reliable reasoning through internal representations of algorithms, enabling generalization to novel or more complex instances beyond training data, with some definitions highlighting formal-language tasks (e.g., modular arithmetic, binary operations) and others focusing on problem-solving in structured environments or Olympiad-style challenges. Disagreements exist in scope, with some framing it narrowly as procedural execution and others as broader strategic or environmental reasoning.
